sections.html:
Oglethorpe County is rural northeast Georgia, with Lexington as its seat, and it falls inside the Athens-Clarke statistical area. Arnoldsville, Crawford and Lexington are the cities, and Maxeys is a town. Philomath, Point Peter, Sandy Cross, Stephens and Vesta are unincorporated. One district, Oglethorpe County School District, runs every public school.

About 16,415 people live across the county's 439 land square miles, and owners occupy 83.8% of the homes. Population has grown 10.7% since April 2020. About one resident in five, 21.1%, is 65 or older, which makes senior exemptions relevant to a lot of owners here.

The Tax Commissioner's counter is at 339 West Main St. in Lexington, and letters go to P.O. Box 305, Lexington, GA 30648. Call (706) 743-8422. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00 but closes from noon to 1:00 on Fridays.

  • Tax Assessors, (706) 743-5166: values, exemptions, appeal paperwork
  • Board of Equalization: Grand Jury appointees who rule on challenges to assessor values
  • County commissioners and school board: each adopts its own mill rate
  • Deed room, Oglethorpe County Courthouse: copies of warranty deeds

That office also registers motor vehicles for the state. Value and millage are not its call: take a complaint about the first to the assessors and about the second to the boards that set rates.

Land, buildings and business personal property are normally due December 20. Vehicles follow the owner's birth month, while manufactured homes use April 1.

  • Interest accrues at 1% per month once December 20 passes
  • Tax still open after 90 days draws a 10% penalty, though a homesteaded parcel owing under $500 escapes it
  • After 90 days a FiFa lien may be filed with the Superior Court clerk
  • A mobile home unpaid after April 1 owes a 10% filing penalty plus 1% monthly, and the home can be auctioned

Bills go to the homeowner and not the lender, so if your mortgage has escrow, send a copy to the servicer. A recorded lien is a public record that credit bureaus may pick up.

Everything starts with market value on January 1. At the county level 40% of it is taxed. Exemptions are subtracted, and the millage rate is applied to whatever is left. Ask the tax office or the city clerk which base and which levies cover your parcel, especially inside a city.

The state revenue commissioner reviews county digests so assessments stay even between counties, and the state's own levy cannot exceed one quarter of a mill. The county commissioners and the school board each adopt their own rate.

sections.h2: How to appeal or claim homestead
sections.html:
Appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. You have 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice, and the letter must name the appeal method you want. Value is the common ground, and taxability, uniformity and a refused exemption also qualify.

For manufactured homes the clock is different: 45 days after the bill is mailed to suggest another value, then 21 days after the assessors' notice to go to the Board of Equalization. Call (706) 743-5166 with questions.

  • Homestead requires that you own the house and occupy it as of January 1
  • Applications are accepted all year, yet one that arrives after April 1 only starts the next tax year
  • Staying put means no renewal form
  • Moving means applying again at the new address
  • Turning 62 opens an added exemption

A manufactured home is taxed on its own schedule. April 1 is the due date, and payment gets you that year's decal. The home's location permit depends on payment in full, so an unpaid bill can hold up moving or selling the unit. If the tax stays open after April 1, the 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly interest apply, and the county can auction the home.

Disagree with the value of a manufactured home? The 45 and 21 day windows described above are short, so move fast and keep copies of anything you send.

sections.h2: What should a seller check before closing?
sections.html:
First get a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner. Then look through the lien docket at the Superior Court clerk's office. Unpaid tax past 90 days can become a FiFa, and it is simpler to clear one before a buyer's title company spots it.

Your warranty deed can be copied in the courthouse deed room. A manufactured home carries a decal issued when that year's tax is paid, and its location permit depends on payment in full.

Homestead exemptions stay with the owner, so a buyer who will live in the house files a new application after closing. Applications are accepted year-round, but one filed after April 1 only starts the next tax year, which is worth telling the buyer early. If you are buying elsewhere, file homestead again at the new house. Balance and decal questions go to (706) 743-8422.

You can sell with a balance outstanding; it simply comes out of your proceeds. Get the exact amount from the Tax Commissioner, with monthly interest and any 10% penalty included, and pass it to the closing attorney ahead of time so the payoff wire matches.

When a bill is over 90 days late, look at the lien docket before you list. A recorded FiFa appears in the title search and goes away only when tax, penalty and interest are all paid. A cash buyer skips a lender's review of that history, which can shorten the timeline when you are in a hurry.

Because the bill comes to you, an escrow account can hide a missed payment. Ask your servicer to confirm the December 20 payment went out before you list.

faqs.q: When is Oglethorpe County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 20 for land, buildings and business personal property. Manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an assessment in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date of the assessment notice, in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. Manufactured homes have separate deadlines.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Oglethorpe County property tax?
faqs.a: Call (706) 743-8422 for bills and payments and (706) 743-5166 for the assessors.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for late tax in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: Interest runs 1% a month after December 20, and a 10% penalty follows if the tax is still open 90 days later. A homesteaded bill under $500 avoids the penalty.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my deed in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: Ask the Clerk of Superior Court's deed room at the Oglethorpe County Courthouse, which holds the recorded copies.
